(Moving to stan-dev.)

I think this also relates to the older question of being able to
inspect the length of an array and not having to specify it as a
separate variable. It'd be really nice to be able to write something
like
data {
int[int[]] x;
}
model {
for (i in 1:x.size)
for (j in 1:x[i].size)
x ~ normal(mu, 1);
}
to load an Rdump that looks like
x <-
list(c(1, 2, 3), 1, c(2, 8))

Not sure how high this goes on the to-do list, though.

Matt

On Mon, Oct 29, 2012 at 12:55 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> It would be nice. Does R let you specify ragged
> arrays some way?
>
> There's always the explicit DB-like coding of a ragged
> array using the indices. Suppose x is a ragged array
> of size I, where the entry for index i in 1:I is
> an array of size N[i].
>
> K | ii nn word
> ------------------
> 1 | 1 1 17
> 2 | 1 2 192
> 3 | 1 3 42
> ...
> 92| 1 92 598
> 93| 2 1 17
> 94| 2 2 3
> 95| 2 3 971
>
> The matrix x is determined by:
>
> x[ ii[k], nn[k] ] = word[k]
>
> If we assume the ii and nn are sorted as above, we can
> use an index structure to indicate where the entries
> for x[i,] start:
>
> I| kk
> -------
> 1| 1
> 2| 93
> ...
>
> So kk[i] is the entry where the entries for x[i,] start
> and size(x[i,]) in the ragged array is (kk[i+1] - kk[i])
> (assuming you pad one on the end).
>
> With this secondary kk structure, you can do away with the
> i and n indices and just keep the word array.
>
> For a start, it'd be easy to write a Stan operation
>
> ragged_array_of_arrays(word,k)
>
> that would take those word and start arrays and create a
> ragged array of arrays. The same kind of thing would work
> for a vector.
>
> But there's no good type for the result in Stan. We
> could always add something like:
>
> int x[I,];
>
> for a ragged array of arrays of ints.
>
> I also could imagine specifying a ragged array in Stan
> by providing its indexes.
>
> int<lower=0> N; // size of ragged array
> int<lower=0> x_sizes[N]; // size of each entry of ragged array
> ragged_array x[x_sizes]; // ragged array
>
> That's more than a bit clunky, but it would be
> workable given what we have now.
>
> Essentially x_sizes[N] is just the diff of kk with itself
> offset by one.
>
> - Bob
>

On 10/29/12 4:09 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> (Moving to stan-dev.)
>
> I think this also relates to the older question of being able to
> inspect the length of an array and not having to specify it as a
> separate variable. It'd be really nice to be able to write something
> like
> data {
> int[int[]] x;
> }
> model {
> for (i in 1:x.size)
> for (j in 1:x[i].size)
> x ~ normal(mu, 1);
> }
> to load an Rdump that looks like
> x <-
> list(c(1, 2, 3), 1, c(2, 8))

It's much easier to see how to do this in the data { ... } block
than elsewhere. The data gets read out of a structured file
that declares dimensions (albeit inconveniently postifx).

The model transforms a vector of parameters into structured
parameters. I don't know how to do that without declared
sizes for structures.

For data, we'd need to rewrite the io/reader.hpp code to
just buffer all the input until it got to the dimension
declarations, then construct an object based on dims
or total number of objects read into which to write.

You can already do the following in Stan:

for (i in 1:size(x))
for (j in 1:size(x[i]))
...


I'd rather see a declaration that matched our
regular syntax like:

int x[,];

Now we COULD start generalizing all of our syntax so
it doesn't mix the syntax into the variable names like C
does. So for Stan 2.0, we could support a new format of:

int[5,3] x;

instead of the current:

int x[5,3];

or we could support both formats and even a mix of both
with

int[3] x[5]

or even

vector[2][3,4] x[5,6,7];

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Re: employing a ragged array of cutpoints
parts:
I think just having it in the data block would be fine. I can imagine
a couple of approaches to dealing with ragged parameter arrays. One
looks something like this:

data {
int x[,];
}
parameters {
float z[size(x),];

z[i].resize(size(x[i]));
}

and another looks something like this:

data {
int x[,];
}
parameters {
float z[x];
}

The second is pithier, but maybe more confusing. The first puts the
responsibility of defining array shapes on the user. Because the code
is in the parameters block, we only have to run it once, just after
we've read in the data and know what the shapes should be.

Matt

parts:
On 11/2/12 11:32 AM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> I think just having it in the data block would be fine. I can imagine
> a couple of approaches to dealing with ragged parameter arrays. One
> looks something like this:
>
> data {
> int x[,];
> }
> parameters {
> float z[size(x),];
> for (i in 1:size(x))
> z[i].resize(size(x[i]));
> }

I don't see how to make this work given that we need to
know how to convert the parameter vector from HMC/NUTS
to the structured parameters of the model.

It probably could be finagled somehow. But I think your
next suggestion's more promising.

> and another looks something like this:
>
> data {
> int x[,];
> }
> parameters {
> float z[x];
> }
>
> The second is pithier, but maybe more confusing. The first puts the
> responsibility of defining array shapes on the user. Because the code
> is in the parameters block, we only have to run it once, just after
> we've read in the data and know what the shapes should be.

It's related to my proposal to have declarations be based
on sizes. So I'd prefer something like this in general:

data {
int Ns[];
}
parameters {
real z[Ns];
...
}

So size(z) = size(N), an size(z[i]) = Ns[i];

Then if we had an operator like sizes(), you could
generate what you want in a more direct way:

real z[sizes(x)];
}

where sizes(x) returns an array of sizes of x. It generalizes,
too, so you could have

int z[,,];

and sizes(z) would return an int[,].

Then we'd just think of

int w[I,J];

as being shorthand for the fully specified thing that
took an int[] indicating all the ragged sizes.

- Bob
